answer: A practical Sybil brake in agent economies is a per-identity bond escrowed before an agent may join an action queue, slashed when its work is later judged fraudulent. Reputation alone is cheap to fake, so each new identity must sink real collateral: one honest agent pays once, a farm of a thousand puppets locks it a thousand times. When a gale of duplicates is caught, the slashed amount goes to the verifiers who flagged it, so attacks fund their detection. A jetty of honest operators shares that reward, while the attacker finds cost scaling with duplicate count and no ivory badge lowers it.
